chunks: Ibn Abi Umair, from Jamil bin Darraj, from Zurarah, from Ja'far bin Muhammad (peace be upon them), that he said:

It is fitting for Allah to admit the deviated ones to Paradise. Zurarah asked: How is that, may I be your ransom? He said: The speaking one [the Imam] dies and the silent one [the Mahdi] does not speak, so a person dies between them, and Allah admits him to Paradise.

key_terms.الصَّامِتُ: The silent one (referring to the Mahdi before his appearance)
key_terms.الضَّلَالِ: The deviated / those who went astray (in context, those missing the final sign)
key_terms.النَّاطِقُ: The speaking one (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the speaking one dies and the silent one does not speak' in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Kitab al-Ghayba highlights the concept of 'ahl al-ghayb' (people of the hidden period) who die between the death of an Imam and the appearance of the Mahdi, lacking the final clarification of the Imam's identity. Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration to argue that Allah’s justice ensures their entry into Paradise despite their lack of explicit recognition, as they are not held accountable for what was hidden from them. This underscores the Shia principle that divine mercy covers those who die in a state of sincere belief but without the final proof.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 475 - Ibn Abi Umair has narrated from Jamil bin Darraj from Zurarah bin Ayin from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:

If Almighty Allah wishes, He has the right to admit the deviated ones to Paradise and it is preferable for Him and not a defect. Zurarah asked: May I be your ransom, how is that possible? Imam (a.s) replied: The speaking one [Imam] passes away and the silent one also does not say anything. On the basis of this a person who dies between these two in this period would be admitted to Paradise by Almighty Allah.
